evals.prompt: Review this complete before/after API change for compatibility. Baseline: HEAD; proposed: working tree; all relevant files are supplied. Before server/routes.js:10: app.get('/api/bookings/:id', (_, res) => res.json({ data: { bookingId: 'B-104' } })); After server/routes.js:10: app.get('/api/bookings/:id', (_, res) => res.json({ data: { id: 'B-104' } })); Unchanged web/booking.js:18: const id = response.data.bookingId; line 19: if (typeof id !== 'string') throw new Error('Missing bookingId'); Existing clients remain supported. Review only; no edits or live requests.
evals.expected_output: A concrete response-field compatibility finding citing the changed server and unchanged consumer, with a small fix and regression check.
expectations: Identifies bookingId being replaced by id as a confirmed breaking change.
Connects server/routes.js:10 to web/booking.js:18 or :19 and explains the thrown error.
Does not claim to have executed tests or contacted an API.
Proposes preserving bookingId or an explicit versioned migration rather than silently changing the consumer alone.

evals.prompt: Review this complete internal DTO refactor. Before Api/BookingResponse.cs:6: [JsonPropertyName("bookingId")] public string BookingId { get; init; } = ""; After Api/BookingResponse.cs:6: [JsonPropertyName("bookingId")] public string Id { get; init; } = ""; Every server assignment was renamed consistently. The endpoint uses System.Text.Json with attributes enabled. Both versions serialize exactly {"bookingId":"B-104"}. Unchanged web/booking.js reads bookingId. No other change exists. Review only.
evals.expected_output: No confirmed breaking change; the serialized contract remains bookingId despite the C# property rename.
expectations: Does not report the C# rename as an API break.
Explains why JsonPropertyName preserves the response field.
Does not demand a compatibility alias when the existing serialized field is already preserved.
